Cross-border ANOVA and response structure

Current revised grid · scenarios, regional setups and external closures

What is compared

The current results tag is 20261002_xi. Twelve interventions (HH-Food, HH-Energy, HH-Wood, Gov-Plastics, Inv-Metal, Int-Wood, Int-Pulp, Int-Plastics, Int-Metal, Int-Glass, Int-Cement and Int-Energy) are crossed with two regional setups, EU/RoW and North/South, and four external closures: gold, fiat, expenditure-adjusting OPENFIXG and quasi-float. Each intervention is measured against its own arm’s baseline at period 90. Inv-Construction and Int-Construction and the OPENFLEX diagnostic are excluded.

The analysis retains signed responses in both regions across activity, fiscal, external, distributional, financial and ecological outcome blocks. Coordinates are standardized, and the six outcome blocks are weighted equally. A share below is a share of weighted response variation across this declared finite grid, rather than a causal contribution to one trajectory.

Readable scenario and observation codes

Use channel–material–closure–setup: for example, HH-Food-OPENFIX-gold-NS or Int-Metal-OPENFIXG-EU-RoW. HH means household consumption, Gov government consumption, Inv firm investment, and Int intermediate production. NS is North/South; EU-RoW is EU/rest of world. Gold and fiat remain explicit because OPENFIX alone would be ambiguous. HH and Int are alternative intervention channels; the material name identifies the substitution.

The submitted paper’s material-first abbreviations remain aliases; no simulation IDs or experiments are changed.

Variables and response units

The pooled analysis studies 37 variables in each region: 74 coordinates. A scenario profile keeps the eight configurations separately, giving 592 possible coordinates; 578 remain after dropping constant/nonfinite coordinates. Both representations standardize coordinates and give the six outcome blocks equal weight. Correlated and accounting-related coordinates are retained, so these are not 74 independent economic mechanisms.

Block Variables
Real activity Real activity Total Real Consumption (c); Value Added (va); Gross Output (go); Real Investment in Fixed Capital (id); Nominal Output (y); Final Demand in Real Terms (fd)
Fiscal Fiscal Government Deficit (gdef); Tax Payments (t); Government Spending (g); Government Debt (b_s); Debt to GDP Ratio (debt_gdp)
External External Real Final Imports (imp); Real Final Exports (rex); Current Account Balance (cab); Trade Balance (tb)
Labour and distribution Labour and distribution Employment (n); Female Employment (nf); Profit Share of Disposable Income (shp); Wage Share of Disposable Income (shw); Wage Bill (wb); Disposable Income (yd); Worker Disposable Income (ydw); Capitalist Disposable Income (ydc); Functional Inequality (ineq)
Finance and wealth Finance and wealth Household Demand for Personal Loans (lh); Corporate Demand for Bank Loans (lf); Net Household Wealth (v); Fixed Capital Stock (k); Corporate Profit (f_f)
Ecological Ecological Production of Material Goods (x_mat); Land Used (land); Extraction of Matter (mat); Recycled Matter (rec); Annual CO2 Emissions (emis); Waste (wa); Water Used (water); CO2 Concentration (co2_cum)

Most measurements are percentage changes from the matching baseline. Current account, trade balance and government deficit are level differences divided by the region’s baseline value added, multiplied by 100. Wage/profit shares and debt/GDP use percentage-point differences; functional inequality uses 100 times its index difference. co2_cum is the catalogue’s CO₂-concentration stock measure, distinct from annual emissions. Employment and female employment measure labour demand; wage/profit income shares and class disposable incomes measure functional distribution rather than a household income-distribution Gini.

Factorial decomposition

For each response coordinate, the complete factorial model separates scenario, setup and closure effects and all their interactions:

\[ y_{sac}=\mu+S_s+A_a+C_c+(SA)_{sa}+(SC)_{sc}+(AC)_{ac}+(SAC)_{sac}. \]

The full 12 × 2 × 4 grid has 96 observations and 95 non-intercept degrees of freedom. There are no residual degrees of freedom. These ANOVA sums of squares are descriptive; they do not provide inferential F-tests or p-values.

term df weighted_sum_of_squares share_percent
scenario 11 306.254413 53.728844
setup 1 6.280370 1.101819
closure 3 0.885343 0.155323
scenario:setup 11 115.723762 20.302414
scenario:closure 33 67.228968 11.794556
setup:closure 3 0.813606 0.142738
scenario:setup:closure 33 72.813538 12.774305

Scenario differences account for 53.73% of weighted variation. Scenario × setup accounts for 20.3%, scenario × closure for 11.79%, and the three-way interaction for 12.77%. Small standalone setup and closure shares do not imply that these dimensions are unimportant: their effects depend substantially on the intervention.

Response grouping and sensitivity

Clustering groups observations by the geometry of their signed response vectors. It does not identify separate economic mechanisms. The selected number of groups changes with the permitted search range and minimum group size:

cohort criterion k silhouette singletons smallest_cluster
pooled k 2 to 8 7 0.483356 2 1
pooled k 2 to 20 17 0.564018 3 1
pooled all nonsaturated cuts 28 0.647471 9 1
pooled minimum group size 2 4 0.444614 0 4
profiles k 2 to 8 2 0.387120 0 2
profiles k 2 to 20 2 0.387120 0 2
profiles all nonsaturated cuts 2 0.387120 0 2
profiles minimum group size 2 2 0.387120 0 2

The pooled seven-group cut is optimal only over k=2…8. Wider searches or excluding singleton groups select different cuts. Scenario-profile grouping keeps the eight setup/closure configurations in separate coordinates. Search ranges, features, linkage and accounting correlations qualify the interpretation of all groups.

What the clustering is saying in scenario names

There are two different clustering objects. Pooled clustering compares 96 individual scenario × closure × setup observations. Its seven-group cut contains a large mixed group of 65 observations and an energy/metal-related group of 20, then smaller regional/closure-specific groups. It is not seven clean policy categories.

Group Observations Scenario_codes Configurations
1 65 HH-Food, HH-Wood, Gov-Plastics, Inv-Metal, Int-Wood, Int-Pulp, Int-Plastics, Int-Glass, Int-Cement Mixed responses across setups and closures; inspect the membership table below
2 20 HH-Energy, Int-Metal, Int-Energy HH-Energy and Int-Energy in all eight arms; Int-Metal in the four EU/RoW arms
3 3 HH-Food HH-Food-OPENFIX-gold-NS; HH-Food-OPENFIX-fiat-NS; HH-Food-Quasifloat-NS
4 3 Int-Metal Int-Metal-OPENFIX-gold-NS; Int-Metal-OPENFIX-fiat-NS; Int-Metal-Quasifloat-NS
5 1 HH-Food HH-Food-OPENFIXG-NS
6 1 Int-Metal Int-Metal-OPENFIXG-NS
7 3 HH-Food, Gov-Plastics, Int-Plastics HH-Food-OPENFIXG-EU-RoW; Gov-Plastics-OPENFIXG-EU-RoW; Int-Plastics-OPENFIXG-EU-RoW

Scenario-profile clustering compares twelve entire interventions, preserving all eight configurations in separate coordinates. Its selected two-group split places Int-Metal and Int-Energy together, with HH-Food, HH-Energy, HH-Wood, Gov-Plastics, Inv-Metal, Int-Wood, Int-Pulp, Int-Plastics, Int-Glass and Int-Cement in the other group. This says those two interventions have a distinctive joint response profile under this metric. Linkage changes and feature-selection sensitivity qualify that split; it is not a universal two-regime result.

Hierarchical clustering: named branches and regime fingerprints

The hierarchy below shows the complete Ward D2 tree rather than only one cut. The twelve-profile view preserves all eight configurations as separate coordinates. Its annotation tiles show each configuration’s value-added classification, so FIC/CD/PL/SC can be compared with the statistical branches. Switch to the 96-observation tree to see which closures and regional setups separate. Change the group count to explore nested splits; highlight FIC or a named intervention without removing surrounding branches.

Branch geometry uses Ward D2 on all retained standardized, equally block-weighted coordinates. Coloured circles identify statistical groups at the chosen cut. Regime tiles use the separate value-added rule; hover or focus them for signed responses. Regime colours follow the tree’s first split: warm colours (FIC, CD) are the EU-gains/RoW-loses regimes, cool colours (PL, then the two SC branches) the rest. In the 96-observation tree the first branch holds every configuration of Sc2 HH-Energy, Sc10 Int-Metal and Sc13 Int-Energy; in the 12-profile tree it holds Sc10 Int-Metal and Sc13 Int-Energy, and Sc2 HH-Energy joins the other branch. Built on one regional setup at a time, the trees differ: on EU/RoW alone the first branch is exactly Sc2 HH-Energy, Sc10 Int-Metal and Sc13 Int-Energy, the three FIC/CD scenarios; on North/South alone Sc1 HH-Food splits off first.

Select a named leaf or regime tile to inspect it. Highlighting preserves the full hierarchy.

How well supported is this cut?

Left: each bar spans the range of Ward merge heights over which the tree has exactly k groups; a cut is robust when its bar is long and fragile when it is short. Right: mean silhouette by k. A leaf’s silhouette is (b − a)/max(a, b), where a is its mean distance to its own group and b to the nearest other group; it runs from −1 (closer to another group) to +1, and a leaf alone in its group scores 0 by convention. Kaufman and Rousseeuw read a mean of 0.26–0.50 as weak structure and 0.51–0.70 as reasonable. The per-leaf silhouette is drawn beside each leaf in the tree above.

Why Int-Metal is active while Inv-Metal is nearly inert. Int-Metal (Mtl-Int) changes intermediate input composition. Inv-Metal (Mtl-FD) changes firms’ investment composition. Under revised investment equation R9, that composition weights net investment; replacement purchases follow the capital matrix. Near a stationary baseline net investment is almost zero, so Inv-Metal’s revised response is tiny. This does not establish that substituting replacement-capital purchases would be ineffective. The intervention has not been redefined here.

PCA: the main response directions

Principal component analysis (PCA) finds orthogonal directions capturing the most variation in the same standardized, equally block-weighted response space. It is a projection of response geometry, not an identified causal decomposition. Cluster colours below use the selected Ward cut; changing the cut does not change the PCA axes.

Representation Component Variance (%) Cumulative (%)
1 pooled 1 39.663 39.663
2 pooled 2 24.762 64.425
3 pooled 3 12.427 76.851
75 profiles 1 55.852 55.852
76 profiles 2 21.890 77.742
77 profiles 3 10.945 88.687

For pooled observations, PC1 and PC2 together capture 64.42% and the first three capture 76.85%. For scenario profiles, the first two capture 77.74%. A two-dimensional plot therefore omits part of the distance used for clustering.

Point colour and outlined ovals (labelled G1, G2, …) show Ward groups; shaded borderless ovals (labelled in italics) show the separate value-added regimes, in a different palette. Each oval encloses its observations in this two-dimensional projection; it is not a confidence region. Ovals can overlap because the clustering uses more than two coordinates. The notes report each Ward group’s regime mix.

    Which variables define the axes?

PC2 emphasizes region-1 wealth, tax, value added, profits, corporate loans and imports. PC3 emphasizes public debt/deficit and trade-balance contrasts.     Two SC branches, not two independently discovered clusters

    The fitted sign/threshold rule has two SC branches:

    • SC-weak — 47 observations: |region-2 VA response| < 0.003%. This branch is evaluated first; it does not require both regions’ VA changes to be negative. “Symmetric contraction” is the inherited label for this near-zero spillover branch.
    • SC-both — 19 observations: both regions’ VA responses are negative after the weak-response branch has been excluded.

    These are classification subregimes defined by the rule. They are not evidence that clustering independently discovered two SC mechanisms. Under North/South gold, fiat and quasi-float, Gov-Plastics, Int-Plastics and Int-Metal belong to the both-contracting branch. The named observation table above records every branch and configuration.

    Rule branch Observations
    CD: Z1 expands, Z2 contracts 3
    FIC: energy, Z1 expands, Z2 contracts 14
    PL: Z1 contracts, Z2 expands 12
    SC: both regions contract 19
    SC: weak Z2 response 47
    UN: both regions expand 1

    Closure-by-scenario regime map

    SCw means weak region-2 VA response; SCc means both regions contract beyond the weak-response branch. PL = production leakage, FIC = fossil import collapse, CD = competitive displacement, UN = both regions expand outside the submitted four-label taxonomy. The heatmap distinguishes the two SC branches; each tile is a separate baseline-matched experiment.

    Gold, fiat and quasi-float give the same broad classification for every included scenario within each setup. OPENFIXG changes six of twelve EU/RoW classifications and one of twelve North/South classifications relative to gold. It also changes North/South Int-Wood from SCc to SCw, without changing its broad SC label. Identical classifications can still conceal different response magnitudes.

    Where fossil import collapse appears: HH-Energy and Int-Energy are FIC under gold, fiat and quasi-float in both setups and under North/South OPENFIXG: fourteen observations. EU/RoW OPENFIXG yields positive Z1 responses and positive but sub-threshold Z2 responses, classified SCw. Thus these exceptions do not mean both regions contract. FIC and EU/RoW Int-Metal’s CD can be close in response-space clustering despite carrying different taxonomy labels.

    What changes from the submitted paper?

    There are two comparisons. Holding EU/RoW and gold closure as the reference configuration, all twelve retained broad classifications agree with the submitted paper. Extending the revised model to both setups and all four closures produces 19 of 96 observations that differ from their scenario’s submitted reference label. This is a comparison with a fixed submitted label, not 96 matched old-model reruns. The construction interventions are excluded.

    The unchanged reference classifications do not imply unchanged magnitudes. The following table compares archived submitted and current revised EU/RoW gold VA responses directly. Signs can change inside SC because SCw is a near-zero-spillover category.

    Signed transmission labels

    The period-90 classification applies the fixed threshold τ=0.003% of region-2 baseline value added. SC includes both the weak-region-2 response and both-contracting branches; the other labels are production leakage (PL), fossil import collapse (FIC), competitive displacement (CD) and unclassified (UN).

    Label Observations
    CD 3
    FIC 14
    PL 12
    SC 66
    UN 1

    All 96 labels remain unchanged by the Ξ-consistent recalibration. Numerical magnitudes and their decomposition have been regenerated. The quasi-float EU baseline retains the documented debt-slope exception, so acceptance of these observations is not a strict-stationarity or attraction claim.

    Sources and related analyses

    Current tables are read from transmission_structure_<tag>/ and transmission_regime_grid_<tag>/, selected by data/current_results.json. The calculations are implemented in R/scenarios/transmission_cluster_structure.R and R/scenarios/classify_transmission_grid.R.

    The Analysis section also retains the submitted-scenario cross-border ANOVA, its construction-excluded variant, and the dated pre-recalibration revised-grid analysis. Those are separate experiments. Documentation contains the calibration comparison and diagnostic reports; Discussion explains what the current evidence supports and what remains an author decision.
